text:
maya (PM): Quick sync — Q3 roadmap item: pricing + quota policy. Need decisions on tier boundaries, soft vs hard limits, overage billing, and burst windows by EOD Fri. Several customers asked for predictable burst behavior + predictable SLOs. Thoughts?

devon (Infra Eng): Agree we should standardize two primitives: sustained monthly quota (tokens/mo) and short-term rate windows (rps + burst tokens). Recommend soft limit that throttles with 429 + informative header, hard limit only for abuse. Also: prefer token-based over request-counts for LLM.

sam (Finance): From revenue side, two approaches: a) automatic overage billing at higher unit price, b) grace buffer then invoice for committed plan only. Overage billing is easiest to monetize but upsell friction. Suggest: 10% free buffer, then overage at 1.5x unit rate, cap monthly overage to 200% of plan to avoid outrage.

li (Backend): Implementation notes: we can implement token accounting in the gateway for hosted; Dedicated needs metadata in agent to enforce. We should expose headers: X-Quotas-Remaining, X-Rate-Reset. For enterprise allowlist, we skip throttling and emit telemetry.

maya (PM): @devon @sam @li thanks. Two product options to choose between for the roadmap PR: Option A (conservative): Soft-limits by default, overage auto-billed, clear billing email + 10% buffer, rollout to hosted only in Q3. Option B (enterprise-first): Hard limits for lower tiers, flexible burst window for enterprise with paid add-on, manual overage approval for enterprise. Which aligns with our OKRs (reduce churn vs grow enterprise ARR)?

devon (Infra Eng): From ops risk: Option A simpler to roll out; less policy branching. Option B increases complexity (per-customer policy, UI flows, infra flags) — 3x more SRE work.

sam (Finance): Option B higher ACV upside but delays revenue capture and complicates billing. If OKR this quarter is reduce churn, Option B may help conversion but slows launch. Recommend hybrid: launch A, pilot B with 2 enterprise customers.

li (Backend): +1 hybrid. Also propose we support a "burst window" config schema. Example: 

```
quota_policy:
  monthly_tokens: 5_000_000
  rate_limit_rps: 20
  burst_tokens: 5000
  soft_limit: true
  overage_rate_usd_per_1k_tokens: 0.03

# enterprise override
  allowlist: ["acct_123"]
```

maya (PM): Great — let's scope rollout plan and launch criteria. Proposed launch checklist: 1) gateway enforcement + headers, 2) billing integration (prorated overage), 3) console UI to view quotas and alerts, 4) docs + customer email templates, 5) telemetry + OKR metric hookup (churn, overage revenue, support tickets). Anyone want to add acceptance criteria?

sam (Finance): Add: test billing reconciliation + disputed overage workflow. Also require alerting on >5% of customers hitting overage in a week.

devon (Infra Eng): Add SLO: throttling should add <=50ms p95 overhead. And rollout kill-switch for 24h.

li (Backend): Acceptance: headers present, decimals stable, and per-customer override in DB. Add an integration test that simulates bursts and verifies X-Quotas-Remaining decrement.

maya (PM): OK — action items: - @devon scope infra work (estimate by Tue) - @li prototype gateway accounting + tests (PR by Tue) - @sam finalize pricing sheet for overage rates (numbers by Wed) - I'll draft docs and email templates. We'll present to GTM on Thu.

ops-bot: Note: Existing quota telemetry dashboard (prod.quota) shows token usage per customer. You can create alerts via /alerts create prod.quota > 90pct.

maya (PM): Thanks everyone. If no objections by EOD Fri we'll land Option A with enterprise pilot. :thumbsup:
